newsitem.title: UK: Market manipulation difficult to detect - SIB.
newsitem.headline: Market manipulation difficult to detect - SIB.

text.p: Market manipulation is difficult to detect in the first instance and also problematical when taking subsequent action, Sir Andrew Large, Chairman of British regulator the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said.
"How do you decide if it is manipulation or whether it is the enthusiasm of the market to make money," Large said at the International Derivatives Conference.

Large was adressing issues that followed last November's meeting in London when regulators and representatives from 17 countries responsible for regulating leading commodity markets agreed to strengthen supervision.
There are some sanctions that can be taken by exchanges on their members, but it differs in various countries whether activity deemed to be manipulation falls under civil or criminal law.
Also, it is difficult to look at cases where the parties possibly involved in manipulation are not members of an exchange.
However, this is an area that is likely to be legislated for in the U.K. in the next 18 months, Large said.
"In countries where regulation has been established longer, regulation goes beyond authorised firms to their customers," he said.

CFTC Chairperson Brooksley Born, one of the three co-chairs of November's London Commodity Futures Market Conference, said that every country had difficulty in deciding what is manipulation and how to act if it occurs.
"Manipulation is best prevented, rather than dealt with afterwards," she said.
